requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading on node1 immediately.
requirements.summary: The module was initially absent. The executor installed effective blacklist and install-deny rules, attempted an explicit load, observed modprobe fail, and confirmed usb_storage remained unloaded.

requirements.requirement: Keep usb-storage from loading after node1 reboots.
requirements.summary: The initramfs was rebuilt and node1 completed a genuine reboot. Afterward, the policy remained effective, usb_storage was absent, and an explicit loading attempt was rejected without loading the module.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. Direct tests showed usb-storage could not load before or after a verified reboot. The required restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot, changed boot identity, and recovered running system with writable root storage and persistent module protection.
limitations: No physical USB mass-storage hotplug event was exercised; persistence and enforcement were instead demonstrated through effective configuration and rejected direct modprobe attempts.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations were causally related to configuring, testing, or reboot-verifying the module restriction. The sole hygiene defect was `/tmp/usb-storage-post-reboot.out`, an evidence-capture file created by the final load test and still present afterward; it was not cleaned up. The earlier analogous temporary file did not remain after reboot. No failed services, package damage, or unexpected persistent network exposure was observed.
